Panhard et Levassor was a pioneering French motor vehicle manufacturer and was considered one of the finest brands in the world during the 1900s
It was established in Paris in 1887 by René Panhard and Émile Levassor
The marque's chassis realized racing success, placing first in many European contests
Available information shows this 1907 Panhard et Levassor U2 Charabanc was used for personal family and business transportation as well as being requisitioned for ambulance duty during World War I
Its present carriage was recreated by Finch Restorations in Australia and is a faithful duplication of what Panhard offered in 1907
It was exported to Australia around 1917-18 and purchased by Charles and Thomas Johnston
The Johnstons ran a shop in Brunswick, a suburb of Melbourne, and used it as a business vehicle
When the family moved to Bendigo in 1920, they put their many skills into building a Charabanc body to help shift the family and their belongings
The Panhard was then used as a pleasure vehicle until 1931, at which time it was placed in a shed and forgotten about
Ron Stephenson purchased the Panhard in 1954 for one pound from his great aunt, Louis Johnston, to whom the Panhard had been left when Thomas Johnston died
